drivers: one owner (the user), one release cadence
strong consistency: ratings and list entries must follow their book (cascade deletes in one transaction)
no package installs or extra infrastructure wanted for a first version
both sources are already single-process Python + SQLite in their code

alternatives.reason: Shelfie's docs describe catalog/ratings/gateway services, but the code never had them; separate databases would break cascade deletes and add network calls with no scaling need
no existing system must stay separate
nothing is asynchronous; every action is a direct read or write
no part needs a second style

style.reason: The simplest design that meets every driver: one process, one SQLite database, modules with clear ownership

stack.frontend: one static HTML page with vanilla JavaScript calling the JSON API (no build step, no framework)
stack.backend: Python 3.10+ standard library: wsgiref server, a small router, json, sqlite3, hashlib.scrypt, secrets
stack.database: SQLite 3 (one file), foreign keys on, WAL mode
stack.hosting: single process on the user's machine or any small VM; not decided (no deployment in scope)
stack.tests: unittest (standard library), HTTP-level tests against an in-process server and a temp database

reasons.frontend: D02: neither source has a UI; people need one to keep a library; a static page needs no install
reasons.backend: D01: both sources are Python standard library; installing packages is not approved; code reuse from Shelfie's handler shape is possible
reasons.database: D01/D03: both sources use SQLite in their code (Shelfie's README says PostgreSQL; the code wins); one file keeps cascades consistent
reasons.hosting: deployment is out of scope in plan mode
reasons.tests: unittest needs no install and is the harness run_tests.py records

modules.name: core
modules.responsibility: configuration, database connection (foreign keys on, commit per request), router, JSON error format, the single permission check can_access(person, record)

modules.name: accounts
modules.responsibility: sign up, sign in, sign out, current person; password hashing; server-side sessions

modules.name: library
modules.responsibility: a person's books: add, list, view, edit, remove

modules.name: ratings
modules.responsibility: one 1-5 star rating per person per book: set, replace, clear

modules.name: lists
modules.responsibility: reading lists: create, view, rename, delete; add and remove books

modules.name: export
modules.responsibility: JSON export of a person's books with their stars

modules.name: web
modules.responsibility: static page and client-side screens calling the API

auth.session: server-side session row; random 32-byte token in an http-only, SameSite=Lax cookie (Secure when COOKIE_SECURE=true); 30-day expiry; sign out deletes the row

permissions.member: full access to rows whose owner_id is their own id; nothing else. Another person's ids answer 404.

navigation.screen: Library (books with stars, add book, export link)
Book (edit, rate, lists it is on)

design_system.icons: none; the star rating uses the Unicode star character

configuration.COOKIE_SECURE: mark the session cookie Secure; default false in development, true behind HTTPS

slices.name: Core loop: sign up, sign in, add and see your books

decisions.decision: Python 3 standard library backend with SQLite
decisions.reason: both sources' code is Python + sqlite3 (Shelfie's docs claim PostgreSQL and three services; the code wins); no installs approved

decisions.decision: One static HTML page with vanilla JS as the UI
decisions.reason: neither source has a UI; no build step or package needed; alternative: API only, like both sources
see style; Shelfie's documented three-service design was never built

decisions.decision: Accounts (email + password) and an owner-only permission model as platform pieces
decisions.reason: the user wants 'people' to keep libraries; neither source has users (compat decisions authorization-model, session)

decisions.decision: Ratings are integer 1-5 'stars', one per person per book, replaceable and clearable
decisions.reason: both apps' code; Shelfie's 1-10 'score' docs are out of date

decisions.decision: Export is JSON [{title, stars}] for the signed-in person; no CSV
decisions.reason: Shelfie's code; the CSV export in its README/spec never existed

decisions.decision: REST under /api, no version prefix, error shape {"error": {"code", "message"}}, no pagination
decisions.reason: Shelfie's code uses /api without /v1; one error shape for the whole app (replaces Shelfie's {"error": message}); personal libraries are small, pagination can be added later

decisions.decision: Commit every write, foreign keys on, cascade deletes from Book to Rating and ListBook
decisions.reason: neither source commits or enforces foreign keys (compat decision write-persistence)

decisions.decision: Start with an empty database; no import from shelfie.db or readr.db
decisions.reason: no data provided; an import would re-key ids and needs its own plan and approval

decisions.decision: Route /api/books/export is matched before /api/books/{id}; ids are integers only
decisions.reason: keeps Shelfie's observed export path without ambiguity
